chunks: The Hajj pilgrim is of three types: the Qarin, the Mufrid, and the Mutamatti' with 'Umra to Hajj.
It is not permissible for the people of Mecca and those residing nearby to perform Hajj al-Tamattu'; they may only perform Qiran or Ifrad.
according to the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'That is for those whose family is not present at the Sacred Mosque.'

The boundary of those present near the Sacred Mosque encompasses the people of Mecca and their surroundings within forty-eight miles. Whoever is outside this boundary must perform Hajj only as a Mutamatti' with 'Umra, and God does not accept any other form from them.
It is recommended that ihram be assumed from al-'Aqiq: its beginning is al-Maslah, its middle is Ghamra, and its end is Dhat 'Irq, with its beginning being most virtuous.

For the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) designated al-'Aqiq for the people of Iraq, Qarn al-Manazil for the people of Ta'if, Yalamlam for the people of Yemen, al-Mahiya'a — which is al-Juhfa — for the people of the Levant, and Dhul-Hulayfa — which is Masjid al-Shajara — for the people of Medina.
It is not permissible to enter ihram before reaching al-Miqat, nor is it permissible to delay ihram past al-Miqat except for a legitimate excuse or taqiyya.

key_terms.تقية: Taqiyya: precautionary dissimulation permitting relaxation of a ruling under duress or fear
key_terms.قارن: Qarin: one who enters ihram for both Hajj and 'Umra simultaneously, without releasing ihram between them
key_terms.متمتع: Mutamatti': one who performs 'Umra first, releases ihram, then re-enters ihram for Hajj
key_terms.مفرد: Mufrid: one who performs Hajj alone without 'Umra in the same journey
key_terms.ميقات: Miqat: the designated geographical boundary station where pilgrims must enter ihram

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of Hajj and where are the miqat stations according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This legal ruling from Shaykh al-Saduq's Amali classifies the three valid forms of Hajj — Qarin, Ifrad, and Tamattu' — and rules that the people of Mecca and its forty-eight-mile radius are restricted to Qiran or Ifrad, citing the Quranic verse 2:196. The text then details the miqat stations assigned by the Prophet (SAWW) for pilgrims coming from Iraq, Ta'if, Yemen, Syria, and Medina, while establishing that ihram must be assumed precisely at the miqat — neither before nor after — except in cases of illness or taqiyya.
word_analysis: the Qiran (combining Hajj and 'Umra with one ihram)
Ghamra (a place on the road to Mecca)
'Irq (a miqat station between Najd and Tihama)
al-Miqat (the designated point for entering ihram)

en.bilal-muhammad: There are three types of Hajj pilgrims: a qarin (one who performs `Umra and Hajj at the same time), a mufrad (one who only performs Hajj), and a mutamati` bil `umra ilal Hajj (one who performs `Umra, then takes a break, and then performs Hajj).
It is not permissible for the people of Mecca and its surrounding areas to do the mut`a of Hajj.
They can only perform the qarin and the ifrad, as Allah says, “This is for those whose family is not in the sacred precincts of the Sanctified Mosque.”

[2:196] The perimeter of the sacred precincts of the Sanctified House includes the people of Mecca and its forty-eight Roman mile radius. Whoever is outside of this perimeter does not perform Hajj except that he does the mut`a of `Umra to the Hajj – and Allah does not accept other than that.

Ihram should be gowned in `Aqiq – its beginning is in Muslih (in Medina), its middle is in Ghumra (on the road to Mecca), and its end is in `Arq (between Najd and Tihama) – and its beginning is best, for the Messenger of Allah (s) assigned `Aqiq to the people of Iraq, Qarn al-Manazil to the people of Ta’if, Yalamlam to the people of Yemen, al-Mahi`a – which is Juhfa – to the people of the Levant, and Dhul Halifa – Masjid al-Shajara – to the people of Medina.
It is not permissible to gown the ihram before reaching al-Miqat, nor is it permissible to delay it passed al-Miqat except for a legitimate reason.
